source.encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › General Multi-Panel Tips
source.texto: **Panel count vs. detail trade-off:** More panels = less detail per panel. 4 panels allow rich per-panel descriptions; 12 panels need brief, visually distinct descriptions (3-8 words each).

source.encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › General Multi-Panel Tips
source.texto: **Subject consistency:** Always include an explicit instruction: "same person / same character / same product across all panels." Repeat key identity markers (hair color, clothing, distinguishing features) rather than saying "same as before."

source.encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › General Multi-Panel Tips
source.texto: **Grid specification:** Always state the grid dimensions (e.g., "3x2 grid, 3 columns 2 rows"). Saying "6 panels" without layout instruction lets the model choose an unpredictable arrangement.

source.encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › General Multi-Panel Tips
source.texto: **Borders and gaps:** Be explicit — "thin white border between panels" or "borderless, no gaps." Default behavior varies by model and is unreliable.

source.encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › General Multi-Panel Tips
source.texto: **Reading order:** State it: "left-to-right, top-to-bottom" or "numbered 1-9 starting top-left." Without this, narrative flow may be jumbled.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis
source.texto: Use this reference when the user asks to analyze an image and convert it to a generation prompt: **style transfer**, **mood reference**, **"сделай промпт по этой картинке"**, **"перенеси стиль/образ"**, **"проанализируй кадр"**, **"image to prompt"**, **"reverse-engineer this look"**.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis
source.texto: The process has two strict steps. Do not skip Step 1. Do not freestyle Step 2.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION
source.texto: Scan the image as **raw data** and extract facts based on:

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION
source.texto: Evaluate the following four parameter blocks.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
source.texto: - **Who / What:** precise clothing (era, style, materials), age, skin texture, makeup / toning, micro-expressions.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
source.texto: - **Shot size (after Mascelli):** Extreme Long Shot (ELS), Long Shot, Medium Shot, Two-shot / Three-shot, Close-Up (CU), Choker CU, Extreme CU, Insert shot.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
source.texto: - **Directing & force placement (Blocking after Kenworthy):** isolating the character at the edge of the frame (anxiety), physical barriers, face turned away from camera, shooting from behind (effect of unknown / powerlessness). Height difference (Level Change) for dominance.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
source.texto: - **Kinetics & perceptual forces (Arnheim):** visual weight of the object, center of gravity. Internal tension of form (compression / stretching / twisting). Pose, plasticity, motion vectors. Imitation of swift action (motion blur) or monumental stillness.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
source.texto: - **Color and emotion (Itten):** psychological impact of the local color of the subject.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
source.texto: - **Gaze:** direction, eyeline anchor, interaction with the frame edges, look into the lens.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space
source.texto: - **Setting & Art Direction:** place, era, background, architecture, specifics of materials and surface textures (gloss, matte, rust).

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space
source.texto: - **Three-plane depth (Spielberg):** clear separation into Foreground (with leading details), Midground (action plane), Background.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space
source.texto: - **Figure & ground (Arnheim):** degree of subject isolation, overlapping of forms, mass relationships. Use of reflections (mirrors, windows) to expand context.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space
source.texto: - **Tonal & aerial perspective (Zheleznyakov):** drop in contrast, desaturation, washing out, shift toward cool (blue-cyan) tones in the background.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space
source.texto: - **Frame geometry:** structural framework (axes of symmetry / asymmetry), claustrophobic compression, surface divisions. Illusion of depth via Foreground framing.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 3. Lighting — chiaroscuro, color and contrast
source.texto: - **Optical & visual contrast (Zheleznyakov):** ratio of lit and shadow areas (OVK). Depth and density of shadows. Exact local color vs. color modified by lighting (valeurs).

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 3. Lighting — chiaroscuro, color and contrast
source.texto: - **Lighting scheme:** Key, Fill, Backlight / Rim, Modeling. Rembrandt lighting, Chiaroscuro. Height, hardness (Hard / Soft) and type of source.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 3. Lighting — chiaroscuro, color and contrast
source.texto: - **Broken light & reflexes (Zheleznyakov):** use of shadow masks (gobos), light through blinds / foliage, color reflexes from neighboring objects onto skin / clothing.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 3. Lighting — chiaroscuro, color and contrast
source.texto: - **Tonality & color:** light key (High-key / Low-key). Threshold Silhouette. Itten's 7 contrasts. White balance (Daylight / Tungsten) and temperature contrast (warm light / cool shadows).

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 4. Tech & Cinematography — optics, filters and film texture
source.texto: - **Camera (angles & viewpoint):** Angle (High angle, Low angle, Eye-level, Dutch tilt). Objective camera, Subjective, POV, Over-the-shoulder (OTS). Movement imitation (Push-in, Tracking shot).

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 4. Tech & Cinematography — optics, filters and film texture
source.texto: - **Optics & DOF:** Focal length (wide-angle for distortion / coverage, telephoto for spatial compression). Depth of field. Rack focus, bokeh.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 4. Tech & Cinematography — optics, filters and film texture
source.texto: - **Optical filters & attachments (Zheleznyakov):** diffusion filters (Pro-Mist, Black Pro-Mist, Fog, Double Fog, Low Contrast) for highlight bloom (halation), skin softening, lowering of micro-contrast. Polarizers (cutting reflections).

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 4. Tech & Cinematography — optics, filters and film texture
source.texto: - **Effects & texture:** Frame format (70mm, 35mm, IMAX). Exposure (motion blur). Stylization (Bleach Bypass). Film Grain, chromatic aberration.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 2 — PROMPT SYNTHESIS
source.texto: Assemble the final prompt from Step 1 data.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 2 — PROMPT SYNTHESIS
source.texto: - Write **only keywords separated by commas, in English**.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 2 — PROMPT SYNTHESIS
source.texto: - Describe **strictly what you see**. Do not invent new objects.

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 2 — PROMPT SYNTHESIS
source.texto: - **No filler.** Never write "The image shows...", "A picture of...", "I can see...".

source.encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 2 — PROMPT SYNTHESIS
source.texto:
```
[Shot type, optics and angle], [Subject, mise-en-scène / blocking, visual weight, clothing and action], [Multi-plane environment (Foreground / Midground / Background), overlapping and geometry], [Lighting scheme, optical contrast, gobos and reflexes], [Color palette, temperature contrast and aerial perspective], [Color Grading, diffusion filters, film stock, textural artifacts]
```

source.encabezado: Brand Packs
source.texto: A brand pack is a single Markdown file that locks in palette, typography, voice, and visual rules for a project. The skills in this pack consume it. Every storyboard, every prompt, every generated frame inherits from it.

source.encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_prompts.py`
source.texto:
The verbatim check is the reason this file exists. Series consistency depends on the
series_lock anchors landing unedited in every prompt, and that is the single easiest rule
in the kit to break, because paraphrasing an anchor is what writing good prose feels like.
A careful authoring pass over a seven-shot storyboard drifted on it seven times out of
seven with every other validator green, and so did the worked-run fixture in this repo.

scope: Prompts de una serie con series_lock validada por shotkit.
trigger: Existen anclas canónicas de entorno/luz/grade para la serie.
interpretation: Mantener sin parafrasear las anclas de serie que correspondan.

source.encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_prompts.py`
source.texto:
The character anchor is a warning rather than an error: a shot with no person in it can
legitimately omit it, and the message says so, so you can confirm rather than guess.

scope: Ancla de personaje del validador shotkit.
trigger: Existe character anchor y se comprueba un shot de la serie.
interpretation: Incluir el ancla de personaje si el shot tiene persona; permitir su omisión en shots sin persona.

source.texto:
Checks:
  1. The header block names the storyboard, generator, aspect, brand-lock, run, round.
  2. The generator is an id in the capability matrix.
  3. The header aspect matches project.aspect in shots.json.
  4. No shot's prompt exceeds that generator's max_prompt_words ceiling.
  5. Every shot block names a shot that exists. A full pass covers every shot; a
     revision file covers a subset.
  6. Rule 1: no on-screen text content appears in any prompt. Text is composited.
  7. Rule 3: series_lock environment, lighting, and color_grade appear verbatim.
     The character anchor is a warning, because a shot with no person in it can
     legitimately omit it.
  8. No duplicate shot blocks in one file.

scope: Contrato de archivo de prompts shotkit/forge, no prompt standalone.
trigger: Se valida un archivo con cabecera, matriz de capacidades, shots.json y anclas de serie.
interpretation: Validar cabecera/modelo/aspect, techo del adaptador identificado, IDs existentes/no duplicados/cobertura, cuerpo no vacío, anclas verbatim y separación de overlays según ese contrato.

source.texto:
The verbatim check is the reason this file exists. Series consistency depends on the
series_lock anchors landing unedited in every prompt, and that is the single easiest rule
in the kit to break, because paraphrasing an anchor is what writing good prose feels like.
A careful authoring pass over a seven-shot storyboard drifted on it seven times out of
seven with every other validator green, and so did the worked-run fixture in this repo.

trigger: Existen anclas canónicas de entorno/luz/grade para la serie.
interpretation: Mantener sin parafrasear las anclas de serie que correspondan.

  1. The header block names the storyboard, generator, aspect, brand-lock, run, round.
  2. The generator is an id in the capability matrix.
  3. The header aspect matches project.aspect in shots.json.

source.encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry)
source.texto: This is the still-panel layer. A storyboard keyframe is not a frame grab of footage — it is a single drawn image that must carry one story-beat with **no motion and (usually) no face**. The animatic hangs off these panels. A panel that only looks good is wallpaper; a panel must report its story function, its drama, and the motion it cannot show, all frozen.

scope: Capa de paneles fijos de animatic.
trigger: El entregable es un storyboard keyframe narrativo.
interpretation: Hacer que el panel reporte función narrativa y drama en un instante fijo, sin convertirlo en frame grab o imagen decorativa.

source.encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 1. What an animatic keyframe must do
source.texto: - **One readable story-beat** — name it in one sentence before generating. If you cannot, the panel is not ready (`dramaturgy.md` §1).

scope: Story-beat de un panel narrativo de animatic.
trigger: Se prepara un keyframe solicitado como panel narrativo.
interpretation: Nombrar el beat en una frase antes de formular el keyframe.

source.encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 1. What an animatic keyframe must do
source.texto: - **One function tag** — Establish / Reveal / Power / Pressure / Detail / Reaction / Shift / Impact / Aftermath / Exit (`role-modes.md` §4). The tag is the question the panel answers. In a faceless spot **Reaction** is reassigned from a human face to the *machine's* face — the needle jumping, the slick wrinkling, the nose squatting. Treat gauges and rubber as the actor.

scope: Function tag de cada panel de animatic.
trigger: Se construye un panel según este método.
interpretation: Asignar una función narrativa; solo en spot sin rostros representar la reacción mediante máquina/objetos.

source.encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 1. What an animatic keyframe must do
source.texto: - **One emotion** — routed through metal, rubber, light, or anatomy, never named (`dramaturgy.md` §2). Mixed signals = no signal.

scope: Emoción de un panel narrativo de animatic.
trigger: Se necesita transmitir una emoción en ese panel.
interpretation: Expresar una emoción mediante huellas visibles, no nombrarla como sentimiento abstracto.

source.encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 1. What an animatic keyframe must do
source.texto: - **One implied motion** — the movement the still cannot perform, frozen as its physical residue (§4).

scope: Movimiento implícito de un panel de animatic.
trigger: El beat del panel contiene movimiento.
interpretation: Expresar un movimiento implícito por su residuo físico en el instante fijo.

source.encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 1. What an animatic keyframe must do
source.texto: A panel that carries a beat, a function, an emotion, and an implied motion earns its place. A panel missing any of the four is a *fantik* — wrapper without candy (`dramaturgy.md` §3). The discipline of this whole file is: **you cannot prompt "motion" or "emotion" into a still — you prompt the physical consequence each leaves behind.**

scope: Gate del panel narrativo con beat, función, emoción y movimiento implícito.
trigger: Se usa el método de keyframe de animatic.
interpretation: Comprobar beat/función/emoción/movimiento y traducir emoción/movimiento a consecuencias físicas visibles.

source.encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 4. Composing a still that reads as MOTION
source.texto: A keyframe cannot ramp, cut, or whip. Each missing move resolves into one of **six frozen cues**. Never write "motion" — write the artifact motion leaves behind. State the cue in the card's *Motion-as-still* field and again in the prompt's camera/light clause; models default to over-clean stabilization and will sand the speed off unless told (§7).

scope: Motion-as-still de un keyframe con movimiento.
trigger: Se adapta un movimiento temporal requerido por el beat a una imagen fija.
interpretation: Elegir el cue congelado correspondiente y declararlo en card y cláusula de cámara/luz del prompt.

source.encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 6. The loaded frame for one panel
source.texto: > **Core law of the loaded panel.** One focal point, one emotion, three working depth layers, zero dead objects. Answer one question in the first glance; reward a second look.

scope: Loaded panel del método de animatic.
trigger: Se solicita panel narrativo construido con este método.
interpretation: Organizar el panel con foco único, emoción y profundidad funcional, eliminando detalle sin función narrativa.

source.encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 6. The loaded frame for one panel
source.texto: **Depth-layer jobs (FG / MG / BG).** Write the prompt in three explicit depth clauses, each with a stated job. This is the engine of "reads in one glance, rewards a second" (extends `dramaturgy.md` §10 into a single still). If all three planes carry the same blur or scale, you have one plane, not three — force a sharp MG subject against a soft FG frame and a soft BG stake (shallow DOF is the panel's hierarchy tool, `camera-lighting-vocabulary.md` §3).

scope: Tres capas FG/MG/BG del loaded panel.
trigger: Se construye panel narrativo por capas de profundidad.
interpretation: Especificar función de foreground, midground y background y diferenciarlos según jerarquía visual del panel.

source.encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 6. The loaded frame for one panel
source.texto: **One-glance + reward** — what it does to emotion: an instantly readable frame creates trust; a frame that rewards re-reading creates density and worth. With no face to anchor on, a muddy panel collapses to nothing. — *in a keyframe*: name the single focal point before generating (tach needle / staging bulb / knuckle), put it on a strong line, demote everything else to support. The second-look reward is a reflection, a bridge object, or a state indicator — one, not a clutter.

scope: Jerarquía de lectura y recompensa secundaria de un keyframe.
trigger: Se busca lectura instantánea en un panel narrativo, especialmente sin rostros.
interpretation: Nombrar foco único, subordinar apoyos y usar una recompensa secundaria funcional sin clutter.

source.encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 6. The loaded frame for one panel
source.texto: **Functional vs decorative clutter — the evidence test.** Keep an object only if it does at least one of: (1) **indicator of state** (replaces the face — tach in the red, white knuckles), (2) **stage of action** (advances the beat — front wheel 7" off the line = pre-stage), (3) **bridge to the next panel** (sets up a match-cut or a reach). Dead detail — coffee cup, mirror dice, dashboard sticker — shows no state, advances nothing, bridges nowhere. Cut it. "Each object is a clue" (Park); functional clutter *loads* the frame, decorative clutter *weakens* it.

scope: Test de evidencia para objetos en loaded panel narrativo.
trigger: Se eligen detalles de un keyframe de este método.
interpretation: Conservar objetos que indiquen estado, avancen acción o conecten al próximo panel; retirar decoraciones no funcionales solo dentro de ese método.

source.encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 7. From keyframe to image-gen prompt
source.texto: - **Render audio as physical consequence, never as a named sound.** "Loud engine" is banned filler (`dramaturgy.md` §2) — prompt "heat-haze warp off the headers, exhaust flame, chassis squat, sidewall wrinkle" instead.

trigger: El beat narrativo implica sonido que debe comunicarse visualmente.
interpretation: Representar señales visuales del sonido, no comandos de audio o relleno como loud engine.

source.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge
source.texto: You are turning structured shot data into prompts that work in production. Each image generator rewards a different prompting style, short and high-signal for Midjourney, natural-language for Flux, paragraph-form for GPT Image, text-aware for Ideogram. A prompt that crushes in one will produce slop in another.

disagree, **the JSON wins**.

build when an adapter advertises more words than its ceiling, or when an adapter never
documents the `aspect_param` the JSON tells you to send. The second check exists because
nano-banana's matrix entry said `aspect_ratio` while its adapter said the API expects
`aspectRatio`; the precedence rule meant the wrong one won, silently, on every prompt.

interpretation: Verificar paridad entre techo/parametro de aspecto de la matriz y documentación del adaptador; detectar discrepancias de contrato antes de producir salida.

Given the same `shots.json`, the same brand-lock, and the same critique, this should
produce the same revised prompt. Nothing in the file format fights that any more: no
wall-clock stamps, no random ordering.

What the format cannot guarantee is the judgement in between. Applying a `fix` field means
reading a sentence of English and editing prose, so hold yourself to the narrowest edit
that satisfies the fix and leave every other layer byte-identical. If you find yourself
rewriting a prompt the critique did not ask you to touch, stop: that is drift, and it will
read as a mystery six shots later.

interpretation: Hacer la edición más estrecha que satisface el fix y dejar byte-idénticas las demás capas.

source.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 1. Text is never in the prompt
source.texto: If the shot has `on_screen_text: "text_03"`, the prompt does NOT contain the text content. Text is composited separately. The only exception: Ideogram, where text-in-image is the reason you'd choose it, but even then, treat it as an explicit override flagged in rationale.

source.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 2. Brand colors never in shot subject prose
source.texto: Colors come from the series_lock color_grade and the brand_lock palette. They get rendered into the prompt by the adapter. Don't write "deep navy blazer" in the shot subject if "deep navy" is already in the palette, that's a duplicated description and produces oversaturation.

interpretation: Tomar colores de brand-lock/series_lock y evitar repetir la misma descripción cromática en shot.subject.

source.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
source.texto:
The series_lock `environment`, `lighting`, and `color_grade` strings flow into every
prompt **verbatim**. This is what produces visual consistency across shots. If you
paraphrase or vary, shots stop matching each other.

trigger: Se renderizan planos de una serie con anchors de entorno, luz, grade o personaje; personaje solo en planos donde aparece.
interpretation: Incluir literalmente environment, lighting y color_grade en los prompts de la serie.

source.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
source.texto:
Verbatim means the whole string, unedited. Not "the same idea in better prose". The
failure mode is specific and easy to walk into: you are writing fluent descriptive
English, `environment` is "minimalist home office, white walls, oak desk, single
houseplant", and it reads more naturally as "a minimal home office with white walls and
an oak desk". That is drift. The frames stop matching, and it stays invisible until you
line up six shots and see six different rooms.

trigger: Se renderizan planos de una serie con anchors de entorno, luz, grade o personaje; personaje solo en planos donde aparece.
interpretation: Mantener la cadena completa del anchor: no parafrasear, omitir cláusulas ni mejorar su prosa.

source.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
source.texto:
Capitalising the first letter to start a sentence is fine, because the check is
case-insensitive. "Minimalist home office, white walls, oak desk, single houseplant."
satisfies the rule and reads like a sentence. Nothing else may change: no reordering, no
dropped clause, no synonym, no inserted adjective.

trigger: Se renderizan planos de una serie con anchors de entorno, luz, grade o personaje; personaje solo en planos donde aparece.
interpretation: Permitir únicamente capitalización inicial según el chequeo insensible a mayúsculas; no reordenar ni insertar adjetivos.

source.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim

legitimately leave it out. When the shot has a person, it is verbatim too.

source.texto: - **Where the body sits in frame.** Which third it occupies. On a piece that composites two eras with a vertical mask, a body sitting on the centre line gets split in half and no amount of post fixes it. This is the single most expensive failure in the kit, and it is invisible until the mask goes on.

interpretation: Fijar dónde se sitúa el cuerpo; mantener libre la línea de máscara únicamente cuando el montaje usa esa máscara vertical.

interpretation: Si el sujeto se desplaza, fijar su dirección de viaje para conservar continuidad.

source.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry
source.texto: - **Nothing that contradicts the camera.** A subject who walks away from camera cannot also keep the same size in frame.

trigger: Plano con movimiento y/o cámara cuyas indicaciones de escala puedan ser incompatibles.
interpretation: Eliminar contradicciones entre desplazamiento, cámara y escala aparente, respetando los movimientos de cámara realmente especificados.

source.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 1. Verbatim character anchors
source.texto: The most effective single technique. The character is described in `series_lock.character` once, and that exact string appears in every shot's prompt verbatim. No paraphrasing, no synonyms, no "improvement."

trigger: Se renderizan planos de una serie con anchors de entorno, luz, grade o personaje; personaje solo en planos donde aparece.
interpretation: Definir character una vez en series_lock y reutilizar esa cadena exacta en planos del personaje.

source.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 1. Verbatim character anchors
source.texto: Even small variations compound. Lock the string. Repeat verbatim.

trigger: Se renderizan planos de una serie con anchors de entorno, luz, grade o personaje; personaje solo en planos donde aparece.
interpretation: No introducir pequeñas variaciones de wording en los anchors repetidos.

source.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 2. Verbatim environment anchors
source.texto: Same principle for `series_lock.environment`. The environment string is identical in every shot prompt. The shot's individual subject describes what changes within the environment, not the environment itself.

trigger: Se renderizan planos de una serie con anchors de entorno, luz, grade o personaje; personaje solo en planos donde aparece.
interpretation: Mantener environment idéntico y expresar solo cambios del plano en subject.

source.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 3. Verbatim lighting anchors
source.texto: Same principle for `series_lock.lighting`. Lighting direction in particular is critical, flipping window-left to window-right between shots produces obvious cuts where there shouldn't be any.

trigger: Se renderizan planos de una serie con anchors de entorno, luz, grade o personaje; personaje solo en planos donde aparece.
interpretation: Mantener lighting literal y conservar su dirección de fuente entre planos compatibles.

source.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 7. Lighting direction continuity
source.texto: A subtle one that breaks scenes when violated. If `series_lock.lighting` says "soft natural side-light, large window LEFT", then every shot's lighting must respect that direction.

trigger: Se revisa una serie con iluminación anclada; un reverse-angle activa la transformación de coordenadas de cámara y su rationale.
interpretation: Respetar la dirección de la fuente de luz del series_lock entre planos.

source.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 7. Lighting direction continuity
source.texto: When a shot reverses character orientation (e.g., over-the-shoulder reverse), update the rationale to acknowledge the lighting flip:

trigger: Plano con ángulo inverso respecto a otro plano de una misma escena; mantener la fuente física y documentar su nuevo lado relativo a cámara.
interpretation: En un reverse-angle, explicar en rationale el cambio de lado relativo a cámara preservando la fuente física.

source.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 7. Lighting direction continuity
source.texto: If you find yourself flipping light direction without rationale, you're producing visual jump cuts.

trigger: Se revisa una serie con iluminación anclada; un reverse-angle activa la transformación de coordenadas de cámara y su rationale.
interpretation: Detectar cambios de dirección de luz sin justificación como posible error de continuidad.

source.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 8. Color grade flow-through
source.texto: The `series_lock.color_grade` string flows into every prompt verbatim. Same as character/environment/lighting. If shot 1 is "warm filmic, muted teal shadows" and shot 7 is "cinematic teal and orange", the audience will read it as different scenes.

trigger: Se renderizan planos de una serie con anchors de entorno, luz, grade o personaje; personaje solo en planos donde aparece.
interpretation: Propagar color_grade literalmente en todos los planos de la misma serie.

source.texto:
Five checks:
  1. _capabilities.json validates against capabilities.schema.json.
  2. File parity: every generator id has an adapter .md and every adapter .md has a
     generator entry. Non-adapter markdown is skipped by name, not treated as an
     adapter with a missing entry.
  3. Prose parity: the word budget an adapter .md advertises must fit inside that
     generator's max_prompt_words, and the .md must mention the aspect_param the
     matrix says to send. A generator whose documented parameter name disagrees with
     the matrix will be called with the wrong one, because the matrix wins.
  4. Self-consistency: a notes field must not cite a word count above its own
     max_prompt_words.
  5. Staleness: warns when the matrix or an entry is past the freshness window.

source.texto:
The forge documents four hard rules and a quality-bar checklist, and until this file
existed every one of them was enforced by a model remembering to check its own work.
That is not a small gap. Rule 3, series_lock anchors appear verbatim in every prompt,
is the rule that produces visual consistency across a series, and it is also the
easiest one in the kit to break by paraphrasing while writing fluent prose. A careful
pass over a seven-shot storyboard drifted on it seven times out of seven with every
other validator green.

source.texto:
Checks:
  1. The header block names the storyboard, generator, aspect, brand-lock, run, round.
  2. The generator is an id in the capability matrix.
  3. The header aspect matches project.aspect in shots.json.
  4. No shot's prompt exceeds that generator's max_prompt_words ceiling.
  5. Every shot block names a shot that exists. A full pass covers every shot; a
     revision file covers a subset.
  6. Rule 1: no on-screen text content appears in any prompt. Text is composited.
  7. Rule 3: series_lock environment, lighting, and color_grade appear verbatim.
     The character anchor is a warning, because a shot with no person in it can
     legitimately omit it.
  8. No duplicate shot blocks in one file.
  9. Shot logic: point of view, direction of travel, scale contradictions, two people at
     one frame edge, handedness in two-handed interactions, brand marks in frame, and a
     clear frame centre on crossing shots.

             and any(k in low_b for k in ["same size", "same height", "two thirds of frame"]),
             "is impossible: the subject moves away from camera and keeps the same size in frame"),
            ((low_b.count("right edge") >= 2 or low_b.count("left edge") >= 2)
             and "second man" in low_b,
             "puts two people at the same frame edge"),
            (any(k in low_b for k in ["high five", "palm", "slap hands", "hands meet"])
             and not ("left hand" in low_b and "right hand" in low_b),
             "describes a two-handed interaction without naming which hand each person raises"),
            (any(k in low_b for k in ["logo", "lettering", "brand wall"])
             and not any(k in low_b for k in ["no logo", "no lettering", "bare", "plain wall"]),
             "puts brand marks in frame; logos are composited in post, never generated"),
            ((("crossing" in low_b or "crosses the" in low_b)
              or "anchor" in low_b or True)
             and not any(k in low_b for k in ["left third", "right third", "centre third",
                                              "no person", "empty", "black frame"]),
             "does not state which third of the frame the body occupies; a body on the centre "
             "line is split in half by the mask"),
            (("crossing" in low_b or "crosses the" in low_b)
             and not any(k in low_b for k in ["centre stays", "centre strip", "clear of any object",
                                              "away from the centre", "far from the centre"]),
             "is a crossing shot but does not declare the centre of frame clear for the mask"),
        ]
        for failed, reason in logic:
            if failed:
                if _is_fixture(body):
                    warnings.append(f"{label}: {sid} {reason}")
                else:
                    errors.append(f"{label}: {sid} {reason}")
